battle.name: 龐勛起義
battle.brief: 咸通九年（868），桂管軍兵變，龐勛率桂林兵北還，循湘贛淮水而下，轉戰千里，直抵泗州、濠州、宿州，攻陷徐州，切斷汴河漕運，兵鋒逼近汴洛。咸通十一年（870）城破，龐勛伏誅。卡面月牙劍並非唐軍兵器，其代表的單刃弧背、砍下不拔一路，在龐勛軍中對應的是環首刀與柴刀。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 龐勛起義爆發於唐懿宗咸通九年（868），交戰的兩方是唐朝中央與其麾下桂管軍中叛變的一支，以及被捲入其中的嶺北州縣與藩鎮部隊。叛方的主體是桂管軍，即桂林一帶節度使轄下的鎮兵與被徵發的南人，領兵者龐勛原為桂管軍將，出身北土，與徐州、泗州一帶有鄉里之誼。起兵之初，叛方只千餘人，多是受命北調、拒絕再往嶺南的桂管兵；北行途中不斷裹挾沿線的饑民、逃戶、流民與散卒，人數迅速膨脹到萬餘，先後攻入泗州、濠州、宿州，兵鋒直指徐州，據城之後，號令所及已達數萬眾，其中青壯為數萬，老弱婦孺隨軍而行，是典型的起義軍編制。叛方背後空虛，沒有穩定的糧道與城邑縱深，補給靠沿途徵發與奪糧，性質上仍是流動的軍隊加上流民團體，而非能自給自足的政權。官軍一方則是朝廷聯合各道的聯軍，實際作戰單位是兗海、泗州、徐州、淮南、忠武、宣武等道的節度使與刺史所領的鎮兵，以及最後由朝廷直接節制、投入行營的精兵。中晚唐的兵制以募兵為主，兵將的效忠對象多在本道節度使而不是皇帝，節度使之間互不隸屬，各保實力，這正是官軍初期屢敗、屢觀望的制度根源。朝廷一方有中央的名義、詔令與調度財賦的能力，卻缺乏一份文書就能調動全國兵力的編制；雙方在整場戰爭中呈現的落差，正是節度使與朝廷、鎮兵與國家之間那道在晚唐已經裂開的縫隙。
countriesEn: The Pang Xun rising broke out under Emperor Yizong of the Tang, in the ninth year of the Xiantong era, 868. The two sides were the Tang court together with the mutinous part of the Guangxi army under it, and the northern prefectures and the governors' troops who were drawn into the affair. The rebel side was built on the Guiguan army, the garrison and the levies of the circuit whose seat was Guilin, and the man who led it, Pang Xun, was himself a commander in that army, a northerner who had ties of hometown and kin in the region of Xuzhou and Sizhou. At the beginning the rebels numbered only a thousand or so, for the most part Guiguan soldiers who had been ordered north and refused to march on into Lingnan again; on the march they took in famine-struck villagers, runaway households, migrants and stray soldiers along the route, so that their strength grew quickly to more than ten thousand. After taking Sizhou, Haozhou and Suzhou in turn they pressed towards Xuzhou, and once they were established in that city their orders reached several tens of thousands, of whom the able-bodied were counted in thousands while the aged, the women and the children followed the army; this was the classic composition of a rising army. Behind the rebels there was nothing. They had no stable line of supply and no depth of towns to fall back on, and lived off requisitions and plunder on the march; in character they remained a mobile column of soldiers with a mob of migrants attached, not a polity able to feed itself. On the government side stood the court acting together with the circuits: the actual fighting units were the garrison troops of the circuit governors and prefects of Yanhai, Sizhou, Xuzhou, Huainan, Zhongwu at Xuzhou in Henan and Xuanwu at Bianzhou, together with picked detachments which the court finally placed under its own command as a field army. From the middle and late Tang the armies were raised by recruitment, and the loyalty of the soldiers lay with the governor of their own circuit rather than with the emperor; the governors were not subordinate to one another and each guarded his own strength. That is the institutional root of the early defeats and the long hesitations on the government side. The court had the central authority, the proclamations and the power to move tax revenue, but it had no establishment that could order the armies of the whole empire with a single sheet of paper. The gap visible throughout the war was precisely the gap that had opened up between the governors and the court, and between the garrison and the state, in the late Tang.
people: 龐勛是全場的核心。他原是桂管軍的軍將，籍貫有徐州、泗州與桂林諸說，多數史家認為他是北方人而在嶺南鎮軍多年，因此熟悉淮北一帶的道路、方言與鄉里關係；他在軍中頗有威信，驍勇而能得士卒之心。咸通九年桂林兵變時，他殺逐或脅走不肯聽命的桂管將佐，掌握了這支隊伍的指揮權，隨即率眾北還，沿途每破一州便收繳器械、驅取壯丁、散財賞眾，把一支被調遣的邊軍變成了能自行擴張的叛軍。攻下徐州之後，他自置官屬、發號施令，又遣使向朝廷求節度使的旌節，朝廷不予，於是戰爭再無退路。與龐勛相始終的是桂管節度使蔡袭：南詔交趾之戰的餘波尚未平定，他所轄的軍隊便在朝廷的調度下再度生變，兵變一起便失去控制，最後被貶官，這說明當時的藩鎮長官對基層軍隊已無約束之力。朝廷方面，咸通末年的同平章事白敏中、崔龜從一類的重臣參與了處置之議，懿宗在位時還曾下詔大赦與罪己，希望以赦免與加官換取叛軍解散；這些處置多歸於空談，兵事仍然只能靠各道自己的刀兵去解決。龐勛本人在咸通十一年城破之後出奔，於敗亡途中被自己部下所斬，首級送達京師，這也印證了這支起義軍在很大程度上依賴個人威望而不是組織的特徵。
peopleEn: Pang Xun was the man at the centre of it all. He was originally a commander in the Guiguan army; the records differ as to whether he came from Xuzhou, from Sizhou or from Guilin, and most historians take him for a northerner who had served many years in the southern garrisons, which would explain his familiarity with the roads, the speech and the kinship of the country north of the Huai. He had a real standing among the soldiers, being bold and able to hold the loyalty of his men. When the Guilin mutiny broke out in the ninth year of Xiantong he killed or drove off the officers who would not obey him, took command of the column and led it north. At every town he took he collected the arms and stores, seized the able-bodied and distributed the booty among his men, turning a garrison that had been sent on somebody else's errand into an army that could enlarge itself. After he had taken Xuzhou he set up his own officers and issued his own orders, and he sent envoys to the court to ask for the banner of a circuit governor; the court refused, and from that moment there was no way back. The one matched against him for the whole of the affair was the governor of the Guiguan circuit, Cai Xi: the reverberations of the war in Jiaozhi against Nanzhao had not yet died down, and the troops under his command rose again under the court's own direction; once the mutiny began he lost control of them and was demoted in the end, which shows how little authority a circuit governor still had over his own troops. On the court side, ministers of the late Xiantong years, men of the standing of Bai Minzhong and Cui Guizong, took part in the discussions on how to deal with it, and the emperor still issued edicts of amnesty and of self-reproach, hoping to buy off the rebels with pardons and offices. These measures came to nothing; the business had to be settled by the swords of the circuits. Pang Xun himself, after the city fell in the eleventh year of Xiantong, broke out and was cut down by his own men in the course of the flight, his head being carried to the capital; that, too, testifies to the fact that this army rested in large measure on the authority of one man rather than on any organisation.
kits: 卡面這把埃及月牙劍並沒有出現在唐朝的軍陣之中。它是埃及自早王朝以來就用於近身格殺的青銅弧刃單刃劍，刃口開在凸面，砍進人身或盾牌之後不必回抽，比直刃劍更早成熟，約在公元前1550年前後的埃及新王國時期逐漸讓位給直背劍與更長的青銅刃器。把它放進龐勛起義的裝備表，是因為它標示的是一條古老的技術路線：單刃、弧背、砍下不回抽的近身格殺。唐末嶺南與江南的鄉兵與日常兵器正走的是同一條路線的末端。龐勛軍中真正常見的是環首刀與柴刀一類的單刃兵器。環首刀自漢代已定型，柄首鑄環，便於懸掛與佩帶，經魏晉南北朝而至隋唐，是南人最普及的短兵器；柴刀本是砍柴的農具，柄短刃厚，前段單刃而略有弧度，砍入人身不必翻腕抽拔。弓弩是龐勛軍的重要火力：弩機最早見於楚地，漢唐之間南方少數民族與山區部眾尤重之，廣南一帶常見的臂弩與擘張弩可以用腳張弦、上弦之後伏於地形射擊，另有架於車床之上的床子弩，可用於攻城與守城。防護上，嶺南產藤，唐人筆記曾記廣南人編藤為甲，藤條交結可格矢鏃，故龐勛軍中藤甲、皮革甲與木牌為主，金屬甲胄尚不普及。攻防器械沿用唐軍既有諸式：攻城有雲梯、撞木與火箭，守城有拒馬、鹿角、飛石與弓弩，火攻多用猛火油與薪束。運輸靠船，湘江、贛江、鄱陽湖、淮河一線的水路決定了這支部隊的行軍方向；民間運輸用牛車，官方調撥則倚賴漕運的舟船。武器之外，軍隊賴以維繫的還有食糧、鹽與柴水，這三樣在缺糧的年份往往決定一支軍隊能走多遠。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card never appeared in a Tang army. It was a bronze single-edged sword of crescent curvature used in Egypt for close combat from the Old Kingdom onward: the edge lay on the convex side, and once it had been driven into a body or a shield it did not have to be pulled back out, so it matured earlier than the straight-edged sword, and around 1550 BC, in the New Kingdom, it was gradually displaced by straight-backed swords and by longer bronze blades. It belongs in the equipment table of the Pang Xun rising because it marks an old line of technique: a single edge, a curved back, and a hack that does not need to be withdrawn. The villagers' soldiers and the everyday weapons of Lingnan and Jiangnan in the late Tang stood at the far end of that same line. What the troops of Pang Xun actually carried were single-edged blades of the ring-pommel and wood-chopper kind. The ring-pommel dao was fixed in form as early as the Han, with a ring cast at the pommel so that it could be hung and worn, and it passed through Wei, Jin, the Northern and Southern dynasties into the Sui and Tang as the commonest short weapon of the south; the wood-chopper was a farm tool in the first place, with a short haft and a thick blade whose front half was single-edged and slightly curved, and once it had entered a body there was no need to turn the wrist and pull it free. Bows and crossbows were the chief firepower of Pang Xun's army. The crossbow appeared in the lands of Chu first and was especially valued by the southern peoples and by the mountain communities between the Han and the Tang; in the Guangnan region the arm crossbow and the pedal crossbow, which could be strung with the foot and then fired from cover, were common, and there was also the bed-mounted crossbow, set on a carriage, for the siege and for the defence. For protection, rattan grew in Lingnan, and Tang notes record that the people of Guangnan wove rattan into armour, the crossed shafts turning aside arrowheads and points, so vine armour, leather armour and wooden shields were what Pang Xun's men had, while metal harness was not yet general. The siege and defence equipment was the standard Tang repertoire: scaling ladders, battering beams and fire-arrows for the attack, and chevaux-de-frise, caltrops, stone-throwers and crossbows for the defence, with fire attacks relying on burning oil and bundles of fuel. Transport was by boat, and the waterways of the Xiang, the Gan, the Poyang lake and the Huai decided the direction in which this column moved; the civilian transport was by ox cart, and the official movement of men and grain depended on the grain fleet. Beyond the weapons, what kept an army together was grain, salt, firewood and water, and in a year of short crops it was usually those things that decided how far a column could go.
tactics: 龐勛軍的戰術可以歸納為一句話：不求守土，只求速度與縱深。桂林兵變之後，龐勛放棄嶺南的城邑，率眾沿湘江順流而下，經靈渠分水、避湘江險灘而出，轉入贛江與鄱陽湖，再順江東下抵淮南，一路上以舟船載兵、以步騎就道，晝行夜宿而不為城壘，專挑防備空虛、府庫空虛的州縣下手。破城之後的處理極為務實：繳取器械、縑帛與糧食，選取精壯編入行伍，其餘的散歸鄉里或隨軍就食；不派重兵分守新取之城，只留少量兵丁同鄉里首戶看守，其餘兵力始終保持集結，以便隨時轉向。行軍途中大量饑民與逃戶跟隨，隊伍尾部拖著長長的移民隊列，這既是實力也是負擔，一旦糧盡即自行潰散。攻擊序列上，叛軍常以數百名先鋒趁夜襲擊城門或營壘，主力隨後湧入，同時分兵斷絕官軍的糧道與驛傳；遇到城池守備堅固則不硬攻，轉而迂回他處。攻佔徐州之後，龐勛改採守勢：四面加築拒馬、鹿角與壕溝，環城布置弩手與投石，利用泗州、濠州方向的道路封鎖官軍糧道，等待各道援軍耗盡銳氣。官軍一方則因節度使各擁其眾而彼此觀望，初期屢攻屢敗、喪師失地；朝廷改為集中調度，設行營統一指揮，把徐州四周的鄉里掃清、斷絕城中的樵採與糧源，迫其坐困，再以大軍四面合圍，配合撞木、雲梯與火攻破城，終於在咸通十一年攻克。
tacticsEn: The tactics of Pang Xun's army can be put in one phrase: it did not seek to hold ground, only speed and room to manoeuvre. After the mutiny at Guilin he abandoned the towns of Lingnan and led his men down the Xiang river, out through the Lingqu divide and past the dangerous rapids of the Xiang, into the Gan and the Poyang lake, and so eastwards along the rivers to Huainan. He carried the troops in boats and marched them on foot, moving by day and bivouacking at night without throwing up works, and he struck only at prefectures and counties whose defence was thin and whose treasuries were empty. His handling of a captured city was thoroughly practical: he took the arms, the silk and the stores, picked the able-bodied into his ranks, and sent the rest back to their villages or let them live off the country as they marched. He left no strong garrison in the towns he took, keeping only a few men with the local headmen to watch the place, so that the rest of his force stayed concentrated and could turn in any direction. Long columns of migrants and runaways followed the tail of the army; that was both its strength and its burden, for a column without grain dissolved on its own. In the order of attack, the rebels would send a few hundred men as a forlorn hope to strike a city gate or a camp by night, the main body would pour in after them, and at the same time detachments would be sent to cut the supply route and the courier stations of the government troops. Where a city was strongly held they did not force it but turned aside and struck elsewhere. After taking Xuzhou, Pang Xun changed to the defensive: he ringed the city with chevaux-de-frise, caltrops and ditches, posted crossbowmen and stone-throwers around it, and used the roads running towards Sizhou and Haozhou to seal off the supply of the government army, waiting for the reinforcing armies of the circuits to wear themselves out. On the government side, because each governor held his own men and watched the others, the early attacks failed again and again with ground lost and men lost; the court changed to centralised control, set up a field headquarters with a single command, swept the countryside round Xuzhou clear and cut the firewood and grain from the besieged city, and then closed in with the main army on all four sides, using battering beams, scaling ladders and fire to breach the wall, which is how the city was taken in the eleventh year of Xiantong.
data: 這場戰爭可以核對的數字分三類。第一類是系年與時間：起事繫於咸通九年（868）夏秋之際的桂林兵變，龐勛舉兵北還在同年八九月，兵鋒抵達泗州、濠州一線約在十月前後，攻陷徐州在咸通九年冬季，戰事以咸通十一年（870）城破、龐勛伏誅告終，前後不過三年，其間最關鍵的圍城戰約打了半年。文獻所記龐勛初起時的兵數在千人量級，朝廷調桂管兵赴徐、泗者亦不過千人上下；北行之後眾至萬餘，攻入徐州前後號稱數萬，其中可作戰之精壯當以萬計，餘為隨軍老弱與逃戶。官軍方面，參與諸道的鎮兵總數在數萬量級，但分散各道、各守本鎮，真正投入合圍的兵力遠少於此。第二類是距離與地理：桂林至徐州的直線距離約一千二百公里，循湘江、贛江、淮水的水路行軍，實際行程當在二千華里上下，耗時約兩個月；徐州居汴河之要，去汴州不過數日之程，故占領徐州即等於切斷江淮漕運北上洛陽的咽喉，這也是朝廷震動、諸道不得不進兵的直接原因。第三類是必須打折扣的推算：南詔交趾之戰中桂管兵的損失，舊唐書與新唐書概括為死者十七八，即十成之中死七八成，此數字明顯是概數而不是點名冊；同理，叛軍的死亡人數、攻城造成的坑塹數量，各家記載皆無可核對的明細，只宜以量級敘述。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked for this war fall into three classes. The first is the chronology. The rising is tied to the Guilin mutiny of the summer and autumn of the ninth year of Xiantong, 868; Pang Xun's march north began in the eighth or ninth month of the same year; his troops reached the line of Sizhou and Haozhou around the tenth month; Xuzhou fell in the winter of 868; and the war ended with the fall of the city and the death of Pang Xun in the eleventh year of Xiantong, 870, so that it lasted at most three years, of which the siege that mattered took about half a year. The texts put the strength of Pang Xun at the moment of the rising in the order of a thousand men, and the Guiguan troops whom the court called north to Sizhou and Xuzhou were of a similar order; after the march north his numbers ran to more than ten thousand, and on entering Xuzhou they were claimed at several tens of thousands, of which perhaps some thousands were fighting men and the rest were the aged and weak who followed the army. On the government side the total garrison of the participating circuits was in the tens of thousands, but the troops were split among the circuits and each circuit had to hold its own city, and the number actually committed to the siege was far smaller. The second class is distance and geography. The straight line from Guilin to Xuzhou is about twelve hundred kilometres; travelling the waterways of the Xiang, the Gan and the Huai, the column covered some two thousand Chinese li and it took roughly two months. Xuzhou stands on the Bian canal at the point where it matters, and Bianzhou lay only a few days away, so to hold Xuzhou was to cut the throat of the grain traffic that carried the produce of the Yangzi north to Luoyang, and that is the direct reason the court was shaken and the circuits were forced to advance. The third class is estimate and must be heavily discounted. The losses of the Guiguan troops in the war against Nanzhao in Jiaozhi are summarised in the Old and New Books of Tang as seven or eight dead in every ten, a figure that is plainly a generalisation and not a roll; in the same way no source gives a checkable figure for the rebels who died, or for the scale of the pits dug in the sieges, and those matters can only be described by order of magnitude.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分成四層。最表層是嶺南的戰事消耗：咸通六年前後至九年，南詔再攻交趾、進窺嶺南，桂管兵被推上前線，山路險遠、瘴癘叢集，舊新唐書所述的死者十七八，把這支部隊的疲憊與怨憤寫到了骨子裡。第二層是朝廷的調度：徐、滑二州的鎮兵久戍嶺南思歸，咸通九年五月徐、滑兵變，朝廷竟以桂管兵去平自己人，等於把一支已經反覆折損的隊伍再推上戰場；桂管兵沿途既無糧秣補充，又不習北地氣候，認定自己只是被送去送死的工具，於是集體抗命。第三層是節度使體制的失靈：桂管節度使對自己的軍隊已無約束力，兵變一起便只能上表請罪，朝廷貶官換人，兵則落草為亂，於是局面從一場嘩變變成了一場戰爭。第四層是結構性的：在以募兵為主的晚唐，鎮兵的效忠對象是本道節度使而不是朝廷，糧餉、裝備與升遷都由主將掌握，這使中央的任何一道詔令都缺乏強制力，也使一次成功的嘩變足以演變為割據。龐勛之所以能一路走通，靠的正是這個結構：他不與朝廷爭奪合法性，而是用速度把中央的援軍甩在身後，用饑民與逃戶的追隨把兵數堆到對方無法輕視的規模。
causeEn: The reasons for the war can be set out in four layers. The outermost is the wearing out of Lingnan by the campaigns there. From about the sixth year of Xiantong to the ninth, Nanzhao attacked Jiaozhi again and probed into Lingnan, and the Guiguan troops were pushed to the front, along mountain roads that were narrow and far off, through malarial country; the phrase in the Old and New Books of Tang that seven or eight in every ten died writes the exhaustion and the resentment of that column to the bone. The second layer is the court's own dispatch. The garrison of Xuzhou and the neighbouring circuit had been stationed in the south so long that they wanted to come home, and when they mutinied in the fifth month of the ninth year of Xiantong the court answered by sending the Guiguan troops to put down its own people, which was to push a column that had already been worn down onto the battlefield once more; on the road the Guiguan men were given neither grain nor pay, they were unused to the northern climate, and they concluded that they were being used up as tools, so they refused the order in a body. The third layer is the failure of the circuit governor system. The governor of the Guiguan circuit no longer had authority over his own troops; when the mutiny began he could do nothing but report himself and ask for punishment, the court removed him and appointed another, and the soldiers went over to the rebels, so that what had been a mutiny became a war. The fourth layer is structural. In the late Tang, with armies raised by recruitment, the loyalty of a garrison lay with the governor of its own circuit and not with the court, and pay, equipment and promotion were all in the commander's gift. That is why no imperial edict carried real compulsion, and why a single successful mutiny was enough to grow into a case of regional sovereignty. It is also why Pang Xun was able to keep going: he did not contend with the court for legitimacy, he used speed to leave the court's relieving armies behind him, and used the famine-struck and the runaway to pile up a force the other side could not treat lightly.
impact: 平定之後，晚唐的局面並沒有因此轉好，反而更深地滑向崩解。第一，財政與糧道：平叛耗去巨額軍費，江南、江淮的稅賦被臨時加派，漕運中斷數月使洛陽與汴州的糧食供應緊張，鹽運與漕運的糾紛更形尖銳，晚唐本已脆弱的財政與糧道再受重創。第二，兵制的教訓：各道節度使在關鍵時刻各自保存實力、彼此觀望，甚至縱容部下趁火打劫，等到朝廷以統一行營與分割指揮的方式重新集中兵權時，局面才扭轉，這套經驗後來被晚唐與五代的高鎮逐漸吸收。第三，歷史定位：龐勛起義是唐末大規模動亂的第一聲警鐘，此後不到十年，長垣的起兵、曹州起的黃巢都接續而來，龐勛開的正是鎮兵嘩變占州據城的先例，鎮兵、饑民與流民組成的聯軍一旦能跨州越縣，中央的軍制就再也難以壓制。第四，區域格局：嶺南與交趾因南詔的趁火打劫而再受蹂躪，桂管系的防務更加空虛；江淮則因漕運中斷而加速向藩鎮與割據者靠攏。第五，史料與考古：這段歷史主要靠資治通鑑與兩唐書的記載留存，戰後的徐州、泗州兩處城址與唐代墓葬出土的刀、矛、弩機與甲片，正好可以與敦煌晚唐壁畫中的護法武士、廣南人編藤為甲的記載互相對照；而較早時期把月牙劍這類外域弧刃單刃兵器寫進兵器譜的習慣，也正是這部戰役檔案要為後人保留的線索。
impactEn: The settlement of the rising did not set the late Tang right; it pushed the dynasty further towards collapse. First, finance and the grain lines. The war cost an enormous sum, the taxes of Jiangnan and the Yangzi were raised by special levy, the interruption of the grain traffic for several months left Luoyang and Bianzhou short of food, and the quarrel between the salt traffic and the grain traffic became sharper than before; the finances and the supply lines of an already fragile Tang were wounded a second time. Second, the lesson of the armies. At the critical moment the circuit governors each preserved his own strength and watched the others, and some even let their men rob and plunder while the mutiny was loose; only when the court concentrated the command in a field headquarters and split the direction of the attack did the situation turn, and that experience was afterwards absorbed, step by step, by the tall and powerful governors of the late Tang and the Five Dynasties. Third, its place in history. The Pang Xun rising was the first alarm bell of the great disorders of the late Tang; within less than ten years the rising in Changyuan and the rising of Huang Chao in Caozhou would follow it, and Pang Xun had set the precedent of a garrison mutiny seizing prefectures and holding cities, and once troops, famine-stricken people and migrants were joined in a force that could cross one prefecture and the next, the military system of the centre could no longer hold them down. Fourth, the regional pattern. Lingnan and Jiaozhi were ravaged again while Nanzhao took advantage of the confusion, and the defence of the Guiguan system grew thinner still; the Yangzi region, its grain traffic cut, moved faster towards the governors and towards separatism. Fifth, sources and archaeology. The history of this episode survives mainly in the Zizhi Tongjian and in the two Books of Tang, and the ruins of the cities of Xuzhou and Sizhou, together with the blades, the spearheads, the trigger mechanisms and the armour plates excavated from Tang tombs, can be checked against the guardian warriors in the late Tang cave paintings at Dunhuang and against the Tang records of the people of Guangnan weaving rattan into armour. The habit of earlier centuries of writing foreign crescent-edged single-bladed weapons into the armoury rolls is precisely the thread that this archive of battle is meant to preserve for those who come after.
result: 咸通九年（868）冬，龐勛率桂林兵北還，轉戰兩千里，攻陷泗州、濠州、宿州，進取徐州，據城不出，切斷汴河漕運，兵鋒直指汴洛；朝廷大震，一度下詔赦罪、招撫並授以官職，龐勛亦遣使求節，雙方名分糾纏數月而兵事不斷。咸通十年（869）春，朝廷改採進剿，詔各道合兵，初期因節度使互相推諉、觀望，數度為叛軍所挫，喪地折兵；其後朝廷設行營統一節制，掃清徐州四周鄉里，斷絕樵糧，封鎖泗州、濠州方向的接應通道，圍而不急攻，以糧道迫其自潰。咸通十一年（870），城破，龐勛出奔，於敗亡途中被部下所斬，首級送京，懸於都市。餘眾一部分降而受編，一部分散入江南山澤與淮北鄉里，轉為流寇與武裝部眾，成為後來藩鎮兵與農民軍的一部分源頭。州縣殘破、漕運斷絕數月、江南加派軍費，這是唐朝為此付出的代價；而更重要的後果在制度層面：這場戰爭讓朝廷看清了藩鎮與中央之間的真實距離，也讓所有人看清一支失控的鎮兵能走多遠，距離黃巢起義只剩五年。
resultEn: In the winter of 868 Pang Xun led the Guilin troops north, fought his way for two thousand li, took Sizhou, Haozhou and Suzhou, moved on to Xuzhou, shut himself up in the city and cut the grain traffic on the Bian canal, so that his spearheads pointed at Bianzhou and Luoyang. The court was shaken; it issued edicts of pardon, sent envoys to conciliate and offered offices, and Pang Xun in turn sent envoys to ask for the banner of a circuit governor, so that the two sides spun out a dispute over legitimacy for several months while the fighting went on. In the spring of the ninth year of the reign, 869, the court changed to a war of annihilation and called on the circuits to join; at first, because the governors shifted responsibility and waited to see, the government army was beaten more than once and lost ground and men. After that the court set up a field headquarters with a single command, swept the country round Xuzhou clear, cut the firewood and grain, sealed the roads towards Sizhou and Haozhou against any relief, and invested the city without pressing the assault, trusting to the supply line to make it starve. In the eleventh year of Xiantong, 870, the wall was breached; Pang Xun broke out and was cut down by his own men in the course of the flight, and his head was carried to the capital and hung there. Some of the remainder surrendered and were enrolled, and some dispersed into the hills of Jiangnan and the villages north of the Huai, turning into brigands and armed bands, and so becoming one of the sources from which the troops of the later governors and of the peasant armies were drawn. Broken prefectures, a grain traffic cut for months, special levies on Jiangnan: that was the price the Tang paid. The more important consequence lay in the institutions. The war showed the court how wide the real distance between the circuit governors and the centre had become, and it showed everyone how far a garrison that had lost control could go; and that was five years short of the rising of Huang Chao.
